full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 229

Sha v. Yuan — dispute over visitation rights

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on May 30, 2024)

Keywords

Civil / Visitation Rights / Minor / Grandparent Visitation / Bereaved Parent

Ruling Gist

Where one parent of a minor has died, and the grandparents or maternal grandparents file a lawsuit with the people's court requesting visitation rights with their grandchildren or maternal grandchildren, the people's court shall adhere to the principle of best interests of the minor and the principle of favoring family harmony, and shall support the claim in accordance with the law provided that it does not affect the minor's normal life and physical and mental health.

Basic Facts

Sha is the mother of Ding. Sha's only son, Ding, married Yuan in March 2016, and in January 2018, they gave birth to twin boys, Ding A and Ding B. In July 2018, Ding passed away due to illness. Ding A and Ding B have been living with Yuan ever since. Sha repeatedly contacted Yuan wishing to see the children, but Yuan refused each time. Sha therefore filed a lawsuit requesting visitation on the 1st and 20th of each month, for two hours each time.

Judgment

The Xincheng District People's Court of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province rendered a civil judgment on June 18, 2021: Plaintiff Sha may visit Ding A and Ding B once on the first Sunday of each month, each visit not exceeding two hours, and Yuan shall cooperate. After the judgment was pronounced, Yuan disagreed and appealed. The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province rendered a civil judgment on September 28, 2021: appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

Reasoning

Sha is the grandmother of Ding A and Ding B, and her visitation of the two children constitutes grandparent visitation. Although Chinese law does not expressly provide whether grandparents or maternal grandparents are entitled to grandparent visitation rights, visitation rights are closely related to personal relationships and are generally based on blood ties. Where one parent of a child has died, the close kinship between grandparents and grandchildren does not extinguish due to the death of that parent. Grandparent visitation is an extension of the parent-child relationship, is consistent with traditional Chinese family ethics, and conforms to the core socialist values and public order and good customs. Grandparent visitation not only satisfies the emotional needs of adult relatives toward minors but also provides a channel for minors to receive more family care. Especially in this case, where Sha's only son Ding has died, Ding A and Ding B are not only the children of Ding and Yuan but also the grandchildren of Sha. By visiting her grandchildren, Sha obtains spiritual comfort, continues the grandparent-grandchild bond, and also provides additional care for the two children, which is conducive to the healthy growth of the minors. Yuan shall cooperate. At the same time, grandparent visitation shall be conducted in a manner conducive to the growth and physical and mental health of the minors, and shall not interfere with the normal life of the minors and their mother Yuan. Communication shall take place before visitation.

Relevant Provisions

Articles 10, 1043, 1045, and 1086 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China
